arxiv-1708-01428.title: Heralded generation of maximal entanglement in any dimension via incoherent coupling to thermal baths
arxiv-1708-01428.creator: Armin Tavakoli, Géraldine Haack, Marcus Huber, Nicolas Brunner, Jonatan Bohr Brask
arxiv-1708-01428.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Armin Tavakoli, Géraldine Haack, Marcus Huber, Nicolas Brunner, Jonatan Bohr Brask. We present a scheme for dissipatively generating maximal entanglement in a heralded manner. Our setup requires incoherent interactions with two thermal baths at different temperatures, but no source of work or control. A pair of ( d + 1 ) (d+1) -dimensional quantum systems is first driven to an entangled steady state by the temperature gradient, and maximal entanglement in dimension d d can then be heralded via local filters.

arxiv-2401-04279.title: Simple Model for Temporal Variations of H α \alpha Spectrum by an Eruptive Filament from a Superflare on a Solar-type Star Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2401-04279.creator: Kai Ikuta, Kazunari Shibata
arxiv-2401-04279.description: Abstract Flares are intense explosions on the solar and stellar surfaces, and solar flares are sometimes accompanied by filament or prominence eruptions. Recently, a large filament eruption associated with a superflare on a solar-type star EK Dra was discovered for the first time.

arxiv-2408-08564.title: Collaborative Cross-modal Fusion with Large Language Model for Recommendation
arxiv-2408-08564.creator: Zhongzhou Liu, Hao Zhang, Kuicai Dong, Yuan Fang
arxiv-2408-08564.description: Abstract . Despite the success of conventional collaborative filtering (CF) approaches for recommendation systems, they exhibit limitations in leveraging semantic knowledge within the textual attributes of users and items. Recent focus on the application of large language models for recommendation (LLM4Rec) has highlighted their capability for effective semantic knowledge capture.

arxiv-2506-12375.title: Optimized Spectral Fault Receptive Fields for Diagnosis-Informed Prognosis
arxiv-2506-12375.creator: Stan Muñoz Guitiérrez, Franz Wotawa
arxiv-2506-12375.description: Abstract This paper introduces Spectral Fault Receptive Fields (SFRFs), a biologically inspired technique for degradation state assessment in bearing fault diagnosis and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. Drawing on the center-surround organization of retinal ganglion cell receptive fields, we propose a frequency-domain feature extraction algorithm that enhances the detection of fault signatures in vibration signals.

arxiv-2510-14718.title: Speculative Model Risk in Healthcare AI: Using Storytelling to Surface Unintended Harms
arxiv-2510-14718.creator: Xingmeng Zhao, Dan Schumacher, Veronica Rammouz, Anthony Rios
arxiv-2510-14718.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare, enabling fast development of tools like stress monitors, wellness trackers, and mental health chatbots. However, rapid and low-barrier development can introduce risks of bias, privacy violations, and unequal access, especially when systems ignore real-world contexts and diverse user needs.

pmc-11351755.title: A Bio-Inspired Dopamine Model for Robots with Autonomous Decision-Making
pmc-11351755.creator: Marcos Maroto-Gómez, Javier Burguete-Alventosa, Sofía Álvarez-Arias, María Malfaz, Miguel Ángel Salichs, Mingguo Zhao, Biao Hu
pmc-11351755.description: Decision-making systems allow artificial agents to adapt their behaviours, depending on the information they perceive from the environment and internal processes. Human beings possess unique decision-making capabilities, adapting to current situations and anticipating future challenges. Autonomous robots with adaptive and anticipatory decision-making emulating humans can bring robots with skills that users can understand more easily.

pmc-11605119.title: Endogenous chondroitin extends lifespan by inhibiting VHA-7-mediated tubular lysosome formation
pmc-11605119.creator: Yukimasa Shibata, Yuri Tanaka, Shunsuke Mori, Kaito Mitsuzumi, Shion Fujii, Hiroyuki Sasakura, Yuki Morioka, Kenji Sugioka, Kosei Takeuchi, Kiyoji Nishiwaki
pmc-11605119.description: Chondroitin extends lifespan and healthspan in C. elegans, but the relationship between extracellular chondroitin and intracellular anti-aging mechanisms is unknown. The basement membrane (BM) that contains chondroitin proteoglycans is anchored to cells via hemidesmosomes (HDs), and it accumulates damage with aging.

pmc-12384167.title: Investigating Foreign Language Vocabulary Recognition in Children with ADHD and Autism with the Use of Eye Tracking Technology
pmc-12384167.creator: Georgia Andreou, Ariadni Argatzopoulou
pmc-12384167.description: Background: Neurodivergent students, including those with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), frequently encounter challenges in several areas of foreign language (FL) learning, including vocabulary acquisition. This exploratory study aimed to investigate real-time English as a Foreign Language (EFL) word recognition using eye tracking within the Visual World Paradigm (VWP).

pmc-12538993.title: Specific plasma lipid species in children are causally associated with kawasaki disease: a mendelian randomization analysis
pmc-12538993.creator: Changqing Zhen, Shuo Zhang, Feng Guo
pmc-12538993.description: BackgroundKawasaki Disease (KD) is an acute pediatric vasculitis and the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, yet its etiology involving lipid metabolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential causal associations between plasma lipid species, measured in a pediatric cohort, and the risk of KD using a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach.

pmc-12628386.title: Evaluating the Impact of Urolithin A Supplementation on Running Performance, Recovery, and Mitochondrial Biomarkers in Highly Trained Male Distance Runners
pmc-12628386.creator: Jamie Whitfield, Alannah K A McKay, Nicolin Tee, Rachel McCormick, Aimee Morabito, Leonidas G Karagounis, Andréane M Fouassier, Davide D’Amico, Anurag Singh, Louise M Burke, John A Hawley
pmc-12628386.description: BackgroundUrolithin A (UA) is a metabolite produced by gut bacteria following the consumption of ellagitannin-rich foods. Clinical trials in middle-aged and older adults demonstrated that supplementation with UA improves muscle strength, endurance, and biomarkers of mitochondrial health, suggesting that UA may be an effective ergogenic aid in other populations.

pmc-12791846.title: A Randomized Trial of a Resilience-Building Intervention in Adult Outpatients With Congenital Heart Disease
pmc-12791846.creator: Jill M. Steiner, Arisa Rei Marshall, Lyndia Brumback, Yixuan Connie Zhang, Thomas M. Glenn, Adrienne H. Kovacs, Karen K. Stout, Chris T. Longenecker, Joyce P. Yi-Frazier, Abby R. Rosenberg
pmc-12791846.description: BackgroundInterventions are needed to address growing concerns regarding poor psychosocial and mental health in adult congenital heart disease (ACHD). Strengthening patients' resilience is one proposed pathway, given its ability to improve quality of life in other patient populations.ObjectivesThe objective of this study was to evaluate feasibility and efficacy of a resilience-building intervention in ACHD.

pmc-13313360.title: Forecasting COVID-19 new cases using NBEATS deep learning and mobility data
pmc-13313360.creator: Amril Nazir, Mohammad Shorfuzzaman, Muhammad Lujaini Lotfi, Firuz Kamalov, Sufian Badawi, Maen Takruri, Abdul-Halim Jallad, Muhammad Ahsan, Jie Zhang, Jie Zhang, Jie Zhang
pmc-13313360.description: COVID-19 is a highly contagious disease transmitted primarily through human contact. Therefore, understanding population mobility is essential for predicting COVID-19 case trends. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning approach for forecasting new COVID-19 cases using a neural architecture called Neural Basis Expansion Analysis for Interpretable Time Series (N-BEATS).

pmc-13473914.title: Exploring the Quality of Historic DNA From Pinned Beetles
pmc-13473914.creator: Daniel Lukic, Malte Petersen, Jeel Patel, Rama S Krovi, Dirk Ahrens, Roland Gerstmeier, Jonas Eberle
pmc-13473914.description: Obtaining fresh DNA samples for biodiversity studies is often challenging. Natural history collections offer an alternative way to obtain data, although the DNA from dry‐preserved specimens of historical collections is typically degraded and potentially contaminated. Here, we tested three standard DNA isolation methods to obtain DNA for genomic sequencing approaches using 20 identical ethanol and dry‐preserved beetle specimens.

pmc-13700232.title: Social protection and climate resilience among informal workers in Pakistan: a qualitative study of the Benazir income support programme in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
pmc-13700232.creator: Maria Ishaq Khattak, Saad Ishaq Khattak, Hafiza Sumayya Shaukat, Syeda Saira Bokhari, Khalid Rehman, Nauman Arif, Abdullah Alsabaani, Zia ul Haq, Hannah Maria Jennings
